r: Include: evolves skills (context mechanism) for coding agents and measures effect and token cost against human-written skills; group (b).

r: Include: agent skills with coding agents and their effect on token cost across agent-model configurations; group (b), RQ2/RQ4.

q: The contribution is a bounded application of established optimization to selecting assurance context for a supplied software-change task
r: IC1: formal optimisation of assurance-evidence selection on synthetic graphs, no coding agent is run and agent benefit is stated as open.

q: We introduce SERBENCH, with expert-reviewed certificates, a track for selection from candidate pools, and a track for retrieval from whole repositories
r: EC6: benchmark and method for evidence retrieval (code understanding or search) for coding agents, not code development.

q: We construct VibeMemBench, a benchmark whose 3,634 trajectories from the target repositories supply a persistent memory substrate
r: Include: persistent memory for coding agents evaluated with matched interventions and multiple seeds; group (b) memory mechanism.

q: we propose StateTape, a context maintenance framework towards the trade-off between the cost and quality of the context
r: EC5: a new technique tested on existing benchmarks (SWE-EVO, SWE-bench Pro) with no new evaluation design.

r: Include: learned skills (rules) supplied as context to a coding agent, evaluated against no-skill and skill baselines; group (b), borderline as a technique paper.

q: We introduced MemTrace, a state-consistent memory system for long-horizon coding agents that preserves execution evidence with repository provenance and validates it before reuse
r: Include: memory system for coding agents compared with baselines and ablations under matched harness; group (b), borderline as a technique paper.
